intervention_label: PRMT5 inhibition (class evidence — MTAP-loss synthetic lethality)
model_system: Pan-cancer cell-line panel (Project Achilles + Project Drive); CCLE pharmacogenomic correlations; isogenic MTAP knockout pairs
n_units: 390+ cell lines screened across two shRNA datasets; isogenic validation in 4 lineages
dose_and_schedule: shRNA knockdown of PRMT5; no small-molecule pharmacology in this paper
mechanism: MTAP loss causes accumulation of methylthioadenosine (MTA), the MTAP substrate, which binds PRMT5 and partially blocks its SAM-dependent methyltransferase activity. Because PRMT5 is essential, the partial inhibition leaves MTAP-null cells closer to the lethal threshold and selectively sensitive to additional PRMT5 knockdown.
key_finding: PRMT5 dependency in 9p21-deleted cell lines was the strongest synthetic-lethal hit from the pan-cancer shRNA screen, with MTA accumulation as the proposed metabolic explanation. The finding nominated PRMT5 as the lead target for MTAP-deleted tumors and set the rationale for the entire MTA-cooperative PRMT5 inhibitor program.
caveats: Genetic knockdown, not small-molecule pharmacology. No GBM-specific cohort in the screen; GBM lines are represented but mixed into the pan-cancer dependency map. This is the foundational paper for the entire class — every clinical PRMT5 program traces back here.

intervention_label: PRMT5 inhibition (Mavrakis companion paper — independent confirmation)
model_system: Pan-cancer shRNA screen across ~390 cell lines (Project Drive); validation in MTAP-deleted vs MTAP-WT isogenic pairs (HCT116, A549, others)
n_units: ~390 cell lines screened; ~10 isogenic pairs for validation
dose_and_schedule: PRMT5 shRNA / MAT2A shRNA; not pharmacologic
mechanism: Independent shRNA screen converged on MAT2A and PRMT5 as essential in MTAP-deleted cells. MAT2A produces SAM, the methyl donor; lowering SAM in MTA-rich MTAP-null cells reduces residual PRMT5 activity past the lethal threshold.
key_finding: PRMT5 and MAT2A both score as selective dependencies in MTAP-deleted cells. RIOK1 emerged as a downstream PRMT5-regulated effector. Two nodes (PRMT5, MAT2A) and a downstream sensor (RIOK1) were nominated in the same paper, broadening the therapeutic axis.
caveats: Companion paper to Kryukov 2016 — published same day, same journal. Together with Marjon 2016 these three papers are the foundational triplet. Pharmacology came later.

intervention_label: MAT2A and PRMT5 axis (Marjon 2016 — third foundational paper)
model_system: shRNA screen + isogenic MTAP-null cell pairs; pancreatic, lung, glioma lines among the validation panel
n_units: screen across ~400 cell lines; isogenic validation in ~6 pairs
dose_and_schedule: shRNA only
mechanism: MTA accumulates in MTAP-null cells, partially inhibits PRMT5; reducing MAT2A lowers SAM and removes the methyl donor that PRMT5 needs to compete with MTA for binding. The MAT2A/PRMT5/RIOK1 axis is the proposed druggable node.
key_finding: Independent confirmation that MAT2A loss is selectively lethal in MTAP-deleted cells via PRMT5 substrate depletion. The paper coined the MAT2A/PRMT5/RIOK1 axis label that subsequent IDEAYA / Agios / Servier MAT2A programs used as their rationale.
caveats: Third of the three 2016 foundational papers. Marjon was at Agios at the time; this work led directly to AG-270 (later S095033) and the IDE397 / IDE892 IDEAYA program.

intervention_label: MRTX1719 / navlimetostat — MTA-cooperative PRMT5 inhibitor
model_system: MTAP-null vs MTAP-WT HCT116 isogenic pair; MTAP-deleted CDX panel (lung, pancreatic, bladder, mesothelioma); patient-derived xenografts; CSF/brain PK in rodent
n_units: Multiple CDX/PDX models (n=5-10 mice/arm typical); biochemical and cellular assays in replicate
dose_and_schedule: Oral MRTX1719; doses across 10-100 mg/kg ranges, typically QD
mechanism: MRTX1719 binds the PRMT5-MTA ternary complex preferentially over PRMT5-SAM, locking the enzyme in a non-productive state only when MTA is high (i.e. only in MTAP-null tumors). This is the mechanistic basis of the MTA-cooperative class — selectivity comes from substrate context, not enzyme isoform.
key_finding: MRTX1719 had >70-fold selectivity for MTAP-null vs MTAP-WT HCT116 viability and produced dose-dependent SDMA reduction and tumor regression across MTAP-null xenografts. The paper is the chemical-biology proof of concept that an MTA-cooperative inhibitor avoids the hematologic toxicity that sank first-generation PRMT5 inhibitors.
caveats: No GBM-specific in-vivo arm — the included tumor types are peripheral. MRTX1719 was lifecycle-managed into navlimetostat (BMS-986504) when BMS acquired Mirati; same molecule, current development under the MountainTAP program.

intervention_label: TNG908 — brain-penetrant MTA-cooperative PRMT5 inhibitor (preclinical)
model_system: MTAP-null cell line panel including U87MG MTAP-null derivatives; orthotopic GBM mouse xenograft; non-human primate brain PK; rodent PK with P-gp/BCRP transporter assays
n_units: n=8-10 mice/arm in the orthotopic survival study; multiple cell lines for in-vitro selectivity
dose_and_schedule: Oral TNG908; doses optimized for brain Kp,uu; survival study in orthotopic GBM model
mechanism: TNG908 is an MTA-cooperative PRMT5 inhibitor engineered to avoid P-gp and BCRP efflux. Selectivity for MTAP-null cells comes from the MTA-bound ternary complex; brain penetrance comes from passive permeability with no active efflux.
key_finding: TNG908 was 15-fold more potent in MTAP-null vs MTAP-WT lines and produced near tumor stasis with ~3-fold median survival extension in an aggressive orthotopic GBM xenograft. Brain Kp,uu approached unity in rodent and was preserved in non-human primate — the design metric for CNS exposure was met preclinically.
caveats: Preclinical CNS exposure looked excellent but the clinical CSF readout in the GBM expansion arm came in low — Tango disclosed inadequate brain exposure as the proximate failure mechanism in Nov 2024. A reminder that rodent Kp,uu does not always predict human CSF PK. Superseded clinically by BGB-58067; the preclinical mechanism work still anchors the class rationale.

intervention_label: TNG462 / vopimetostat — peripheral MTA-cooperative PRMT5 inhibitor
model_system: HAP1 MTAP-null and MTAP-WT isogenic pair; CDX and PDX panel (pancreatic, NSCLC, mesothelioma, bladder); rodent and dog PK
n_units: n=8-10 mice/arm in efficacy studies; multiple PDX lineages
dose_and_schedule: Oral TNG462, daily; doses across 10-100 mg/kg
mechanism: Same MTA-cooperative mechanism as TNG908 but optimized for potency and peripheral PK (T1/2 >24 h supporting QD dosing). Brain penetration is intentionally low — TNG462 is the peripheral follow-on after TNG908 disclosed CNS limitations.
key_finding: TNG462 has biochemical Ki estimated at ≤300 fM and 45-fold selectivity for MTAP-null cells; produces regressions in pancreatic, NSCLC, mesothelioma, and bladder PDX models. Combination with KRAS G12C and EGFR inhibitors gave deeper regressions than either agent alone.
caveats: Explicitly NOT a CNS asset — the TNG462 clinical protocol excludes primary CNS tumors. Relevant to the case only as the combination partner in the Servier S095035 + TNG462 trial (NCT06188702), where the small-molecule MAT2A partner may carry the activity into GBM-eligible cohorts.

intervention_label: AMG 193 / anvumetostat — MTA-cooperative PRMT5 inhibitor (preclinical)
model_system: MTAP-null CDX and PDX panel across multiple lineages (lung, pancreatic, biliary); isogenic MTAP knockout pairs; normal hematopoietic lineage assays
n_units: Multiple PDX/CDX models, n=8-10 mice/arm typical
control_arm: MTAP-WT isogenic; vehicle; first-generation non-selective PRMT5 inhibitor comparators in some assays
dose_and_schedule: Oral AMG 193, QD/BID schedules; doses optimized to plasma SDMA suppression
mechanism: MTA-cooperative PRMT5 binding. The selectivity advantage over first-generation PRMT5 inhibitors (GSK3326595, JNJ-64619178) translates to a preserved normal-hematopoiesis profile — the hematologic toxicity that capped the dose of earlier compounds is largely absent.
key_finding: Robust antitumor activity across MTAP-null xenografts; no impact on normal hematopoietic cell lineages at efficacious doses. Synergy with chemotherapy and with the KRAS G12C inhibitor sotorasib in combination studies. SDMA reduction tracks tumor response and is the proposed pharmacodynamic biomarker.
caveats: No GBM-specific in-vivo arm. AMG 193 is not optimized for CNS penetration — the Part 1m glioma cohort in MTAPESTRY 101 is the empirical test. The preclinical work anchors the broader MTA-cooperative class safety profile, which informs why BGB-58067 (brain-penetrant successor with the same MTA-cooperative mechanism) is the lead asset for this patient.

intervention_label: PRMT5 + MAT2A combined inhibition in MTAP-null glioma (dedicated glioma study)
model_system: MTAP-null vs MTAP-WT glioma cell lines (U87, U251, primary patient-derived); orthotopic mouse glioma xenograft
n_units: Multiple cell lines; in-vivo arm n=6-8 mice/group
dose_and_schedule: Combination of GSK3326595 (PRMT5i) + AG-270/IDE397-class MAT2A inhibitor; doses titrated for tolerability
mechanism: Combined PRMT5 and MAT2A inhibition in MTAP-deficient glioma produces deeper suppression of SDMA than either agent alone — MAT2A inhibition lowers SAM so MTA wins the binding competition, while PRMT5 inhibitor occupies the active site directly. Two complementary nodes squeeze the same axis from both sides.
key_finding: Combined PRMT5 + MAT2A inhibition gave strong synthetic lethality in MTAP-homozygous-deficient glioma cells; the combination outperformed either agent alone in vitro and extended survival in orthotopic models. This is the closest published preclinical evidence to the Servier S095035 + TNG462 combination rationale.
caveats: Newer paper (May 2025) — replication outside the Soochow group not yet published. In-vivo arm uses xenografts in immunocompromised mice, not syngeneic immunocompetent models, so the immune-context biology is not addressed. The direct relevance to the patient is that this is the only dedicated PRMT5 + MAT2A combination study in MTAP-null glioma models published to date.

intervention_label: AG-270 (S095033) — first-in-class MAT2A inhibitor
model_system: Isogenic MTAP knockout cell pairs across multiple lineages; MTAP-deleted PDX and CDX panel; RNA-seq and splicing analysis
n_units: Multiple PDX/CDX models; n=8-10 mice/arm in efficacy studies
dose_and_schedule: AG-270 oral, daily; doses titrated to intracellular SAM reduction
mechanism: AG-270 is a substrate-noncompetitive allosteric MAT2A inhibitor that blocks SAM release from the active site. Lowering SAM in MTA-rich MTAP-null cells removes the methyl donor PRMT5 needs to compete with MTA, collapsing residual PRMT5 activity below the lethal threshold. Downstream: PRMT5-dependent intron retention and DNA-damage accumulation.
key_finding: AG-270 reduced intracellular SAM with IC50 ~50 nM and selectively suppressed proliferation of MTAP-deleted cells and PDX tumors. Splicing defects and DNA damage were the proposed cell-biology consequences. AG-270 became S095033; the clinical phase 1 (Nat Commun 2024) was the first MAT2A inhibitor to translate.
caveats: No GBM-specific arm. AG-270 had clinical hepatotoxicity and was reformulated; the IDE397 / S095035 / IDE892 successors carry the cleaner mechanism forward. The paper is the foundational MAT2A pharmacology work that anchors the entire downstream class.

intervention_label: Abemaciclib brain penetration and orthotopic glioma activity
model_system: Rat orthotopic U87MG GBM xenograft; rodent plasma + brain PK; in-vitro BBB transporter assays (P-gp, BCRP)
n_units: n=8-10 rats/arm in survival studies; transporter assays in replicate
control_arm: Vehicle; head-to-head with palbociclib in some comparisons
dose_and_schedule: Abemaciclib oral, 25-100 mg/kg daily x 21-28 days; palbociclib comparator at matched doses
mechanism: Abemaciclib is a weak P-gp/BCRP substrate, unlike palbociclib (which is a strong P-gp substrate), so unbound brain concentrations of abemaciclib reach pharmacologically active levels with normal BBB. The CDK4/6 inhibition itself blocks Rb phosphorylation and arrests CDKN2A-loss/Rb-intact tumors at the G1/S checkpoint.
key_finding: Abemaciclib monotherapy at 40 and 80 mg/kg daily extended median survival by ~8 and 12 days vs vehicle in the rat orthotopic U87MG model; unbound brain exposures exceeded CDK4/6 Ki values. Palbociclib head-to-head reached brain levels too but at much higher doses and shorter dwell times. The paper is the proof that abemaciclib is the CNS-deployable CDK4/6 inhibitor.
caveats: U87MG is a long-established but criticized GBM line — it has lost much of its parental-tumor signature over decades of passage and is not strictly CDKN2A-null in all sublines. The PK and BBB data are robust regardless; the survival benefit is the part to read with the cell-line caveat. PDX validation came later in the Sahebjam / Wen INSIGhT preclinical lead-in.

intervention_label: Palbociclib BBB efflux limits orthotopic activity (the Taal 2018 mechanism)
journal: Molecular Cancer Therapeutics / J Pharmacol Exp Ther
model_system: Transgenic P-gp / BCRP knockout mice; orthotopic GBM22 PDX intracranial vs flank; PK in WT vs knockout brain
n_units: n=6-10 mice/arm across genotypes and tumor sites
control_arm: WT mice; flank vs intracranial implantation matched
dose_and_schedule: Palbociclib oral; ± elacridar (P-gp/BCRP inhibitor) co-administration
mechanism: Palbociclib is a strong substrate for both P-gp and BCRP. Active efflux at the BBB strips drug from brain parenchyma — steady-state brain exposure was ~115-fold higher in transporter-deficient mice than in WT, and elacridar partially rescued WT brain levels.
key_finding: Palbociclib was efficacious against GBM22 implanted in the flank but failed against the same line implanted intracranially in WT mice; the failure tracked precisely to inadequate brain drug delivery via P-gp/BCRP efflux. This is the mechanistic explanation for the Taal 2018 clinical futility readout — wrong drug for the location, right pathway.
caveats: The companion Brastianos / Vogelbaum work confirmed the same in independent models. The lesson — CDK4/6 inhibitor choice for CNS tumors is gated by BBB transporter pharmacology, not by potency at the kinase. Abemaciclib and ribociclib both clear; palbociclib does not.

intervention_label: PD-0332991 (palbociclib) in INK4a-ARF-null orthotopic glioma
model_system: U87MG (INK4a-ARF-null) and GBM39 intracranial xenograft; flank xenograft for comparison
n_units: n=8-10 mice/arm
dose_and_schedule: PD-0332991 oral 150 mg/kg daily
mechanism: INK4a/ARF (CDKN2A) loss derepresses CDK4/6, which phosphorylates Rb and drives G1/S transition. CDK4/6 inhibition reimposes the checkpoint in Rb-intact tumors.
key_finding: Palbociclib arrested growth of INK4a-ARF-null orthotopic U87MG xenografts and extended survival modestly. The paper is one of the first proofs that CDK4/6 inhibition has activity against CDKN2A-null intracranial glioma — though the orthotopic effect was substantially weaker than the flank effect, foreshadowing the BBB-efflux explanation that Parrish 2015 nailed down.
caveats: Early-era study — uses U87MG, predates the BBB-efflux literature. The signal is real but weaker than expected from the genetics, which Parrish 2015 later explained mechanistically.

intervention_label: CDK4/6 inhibition is subtype-selective in GBM stem cells
model_system: Patient-derived glioblastoma stem cell (GSC) cultures across proneural / mesenchymal / classical subtypes; orthotopic mouse xenograft
n_units: Multiple GSC lines (n=12+); n=8-10 mice/arm orthotopic
dose_and_schedule: Palbociclib in vitro IC50 panel + in vivo daily oral dosing
mechanism: Proneural GSCs express higher CDK6 and have intact Rb1, putting them in the canonical CDK4/6-inhibitor-sensitive zone. CDK4-overexpressing / Rb1-null lines are resistant. Subtype matters: same drug, different response by transcriptional state.
key_finding: Palbociclib preferentially inhibited proneural GSCs in vitro and extended survival in a proneural-line orthotopic xenograft. Importantly, treatment also pushed proneural GSCs toward a mesenchymal expression program — a hint that CDK4/6 inhibition may select for or induce the more aggressive subtype on prolonged therapy.
caveats: Uses palbociclib (the BBB-poor compound) — the in-vivo orthotopic signal is more impressive than the Parrish 2015 work would predict, possibly because of the proneural-line bias. The proneural-to-mesenchymal shift on therapy is the part to carry forward; it predicts that monotherapy CDK4/6 inhibition may have a built-in resistance trajectory.

intervention_label: Ribociclib CNS penetration in recurrent GBM (phase 0 PK/PD)
model_system: Phase 0 trial in recurrent GBM with intraoperative tumor sampling; matched plasma and tumor PK; Rb phosphorylation as PD readout
n_units: n=12 patients (3 surgical + 9 expansion)
dose_and_schedule: Ribociclib 600 mg PO daily x 8 days, with intratumoral sampling at surgery
mechanism: Ribociclib is a CDK4/6 inhibitor with lower P-gp affinity than palbociclib but higher than abemaciclib. The phase 0 design measured whether intratumoral concentrations exceeded the in-vitro Ki — the only way to confirm that a CDK4/6 inhibitor is reaching its target in human GBM.
key_finding: Ribociclib reached pharmacologically active concentrations in both enhancing and non-enhancing tumor regions and produced measurable inhibition of Rb phosphorylation. This is the first human PK/PD demonstration that a CDK4/6 inhibitor can engage its target in GBM tissue.
caveats: Phase 0 — designed for PK/PD, not efficacy. The Rb phosphorylation suppression was target engagement, not tumor response. Bridges the rodent preclinical (Raub 2015) and the clinical-activity question (INSIGhT / Wen NCT02981940). Confirms that ribociclib joins abemaciclib as the CDK4/6 inhibitor pair with adequate CNS exposure; palbociclib falls off the list.

intervention_label: CDKN2A/B homozygous deletion sensitizes IDH-mutant glioma to CDK4/6 inhibition
exclusion_reason: Population is IDH-mutant glioma, not the patient's IDH-wildtype GBM. The CDKN2A loss × CDK4/6i sensitivity logic is the same but the tumor biology is materially different; the patient's IDH-WT axis is covered by Li 2017 and Parrish 2015. Logged for audit trail.

intervention_label: PRMT5 inhibition disrupts splicing and stemness in GBM stem cells
model_system: 46 patient-derived GBM stem cell cultures (proneural, mesenchymal, classical); orthotopic mouse xenografts; transcriptome + splicing analysis
n_units: 46 GSC lines; n=8-10 mice/arm in vivo
dose_and_schedule: GSK591 (Type II PRMT5i) and LLY-283 (Type I PRMT5i); in-vitro IC50 panel; in-vivo oral LLY-283 daily
mechanism: PRMT5 catalyzes symmetric dimethylation of arginine in splicing-factor proteins; inhibition broadly disrupts pre-mRNA splicing, especially of cell-cycle genes. GBM stem cells are particularly sensitive because they rely on PRMT5-dependent splicing for self-renewal.
key_finding: PRMT5 inhibition (both Type I and Type II) suppressed proliferation across the 46-GSC panel, with proneural lines most sensitive. Widespread splicing changes — particularly intron retention in cell-cycle regulators — were the dominant transcriptome signature. LLY-283 is brain-penetrant and extended survival in orthotopic GSC xenografts.
caveats: Does not require MTAP loss for sensitivity — the dependency was broader. That weakens the case that PRMT5 inhibition is selective in MTAP-null GBM, but the MTA-cooperative drugs (TNG908 / AMG 193 / BGB-58067) restore the MTAP-selective therapeutic window. This paper is the strongest published GBM-specific PRMT5-inhibition dataset and is the model for why the brain-penetrant MTA-cooperative class is the right shape of drug.

intervention_label: PRMT5 as a druggable target in GBM (Banasavadi-Siddegowda)
model_system: GBM neurospheres (patient-derived); orthotopic mouse xenograft
n_units: Multiple neurosphere lines; n=8 mice/arm in vivo
dose_and_schedule: EPZ015666 (PRMT5i) in vitro; shRNA knockdown in vivo
mechanism: PRMT5 is overexpressed in GBM and supports tumor cell survival, partly through E2F1 and p53 pathway methylation. Knockdown or inhibition reduces self-renewal and induces apoptosis in neurospheres.
key_finding: PRMT5 knockdown or pharmacologic inhibition (EPZ015666) suppressed GBM neurosphere growth in vitro and prolonged survival in orthotopic xenografts. The paper helped establish PRMT5 as a GBM-relevant target — preceded the MTAP-deletion synthetic-lethality wave and motivated the GBM-focused successor drugs.
caveats: Uses first-generation PRMT5 inhibitor (EPZ015666) without MTAP selectivity — the off-target hematologic toxicity that capped EPZ015666's clinical dose is the reason MTA-cooperative successors became necessary. Mechanism evidence holds; drug specifically does not translate.

intervention_label: EGFRvIII mCAR T-cell therapy cures intracerebral glioma (foundational preclinical)
model_system: Fully immunocompetent C57BL/6 mouse with syngeneic SMA-560 / KR158 intracerebral glioma engineered to express EGFRvIII; third-generation EGFRvIII-specific murine CAR
n_units: n=8-10 mice/arm across multiple efficacy experiments
control_arm: Untransduced T cells; irrelevant CAR; vehicle
dose_and_schedule: Single IV infusion of EGFRvIII mCAR T cells, dose-escalated; some experiments with lymphodepletion preconditioning
mechanism: Third-generation CAR (CD28 + 4-1BB) targeting EGFRvIII — a tumor-specific neoantigen with no normal-tissue expression. Engineered T cells traffic to the CNS, lyse EGFRvIII+ cells, and (the surprise finding) generate host immunity against EGFRvIII-negative tumor antigens via epitope spreading.
key_finding: At elevated doses, EGFRvIII mCAR T cells cured all mice with established intracerebral glioma. Cured mice were resistant to rechallenge with EGFRvIII-negative tumors, implying epitope spreading and durable host immunity. The paper is the preclinical foundation for the Penn EGFRvIII CAR-T (O'Rourke 2017 STM) and the entire EGFRvIII-directed cellular-therapy program.
caveats: Syngeneic mouse model with engineered EGFRvIII expression — homogeneous antigen expression, unlike human GBM where EGFRvIII is heterogeneous within tumor (Nathanson 2014). The dramatic cure rate did not translate fully to human trials, where antigen escape limited durability. Still the right preclinical proof of concept.

intervention_label: Humanized EGFRvIII CAR-T validation (Penn — the construct used in O'Rourke 2017)
model_system: Humanized scFv panel screened against EGFRvIII vs WT EGFR; NSG mouse with U87-EGFRvIII subcutaneous and orthotopic xenograft
n_units: Multiple scFv clones tested; n=8-10 mice/arm in xenograft validation
control_arm: Empty CAR or untransduced T cells
dose_and_schedule: IV CAR-T infusion in NSG xenograft; lymphodepletion in some arms
mechanism: The team generated a panel of humanized scFvs and selected a low-affinity binder specific for EGFRvIII over WT EGFR — the affinity tuning is what prevents on-target/off-tumor activity against normal EGFR-expressing skin, gut, and lung. Then incorporated into a second-generation CAR.
key_finding: The humanized EGFRvIII CAR-T controlled xenogeneic human EGFRvIII+ glioblastoma in NSG mice and showed minimal cross-reactivity with WT EGFR-expressing tissues at clinically relevant doses. The construct went directly into the NCT02209376 phase 1 (Penn) that O'Rourke 2017 STM reported.
caveats: NSG mice have no functional immune system, so the tumor-microenvironment immunosuppression seen in the human trial (intratumoral PD-L1, IDO, Tregs in O'Rourke 2017) is absent in the model. The xenograft validation is necessary but not sufficient — the clinical activity was substantially lower than the preclinical signal would predict.

intervention_label: CAR-T secreting bispecific T-cell engagers (TEAMs) — preclinical of the MGH construct
model_system: NSG mouse intracranial U87-EGFRvIII / WT EGFR mixed xenograft; antigen-heterogeneous tumor model
n_units: n=8-10 mice/arm
control_arm: EGFRvIII CAR-T without TEAM secretion; untransduced T cells
dose_and_schedule: Single intracranial CAR-T-TEAM infusion
mechanism: CAR targets EGFRvIII directly through the CAR; the engineered T cells also secrete a CD3 x WT-EGFR bispecific antibody (the TEAM) that redirects endogenous T cells against neighboring EGFRvIII-negative, WT-EGFR-positive tumor cells. The TEAM solves the antigen-escape problem the O'Rourke 2017 trial exposed.
key_finding: CAR-T-TEAM cells eradicated mixed antigen-heterogeneous intracranial tumors that single-target EGFRvIII CAR-T cells could not. The paper is the direct preclinical blueprint for the Choi 2024 NEJM CARv3-TEAM-E first-in-human readout — which showed dramatic radiographic responses on the same logic.
caveats: Xenograft only, no syngeneic / immunocompetent arm. WT EGFR is not expressed in normal mouse brain in the model, so the on-target/off-tumor risk for human CNS (normal mouse brain has low WT-EGFR but human brain endothelium does) is not tested. Intraventricular delivery in the clinical trial mitigates systemic exposure but the design caveat is real.

intervention_label: O'Rourke 2017 STM (clinical paper with preclinical adaptive-resistance correlates)
exclusion_reason: Already captured as a clinical-evidence row (gbm-mtap-c4bq-egfrviii-orourke-2017-stm). The intratumoral correlative biology (PD-L1, IDO, Treg upregulation post-CAR-T) is genuinely preclinical in feel but the paper is a clinical phase 1 with paired-tissue analysis, so it belongs to the clinical dossier.

intervention_label: EGFRvIII heterogeneity within GBM (the resistance biology)
model_system: Multi-region tumor sampling from 18 primary EGFR-amplified GBMs; FISH and IHC for EGFRvIII; single-cell-level antigen mapping
n_units: 18 primary tumors; 3-5 regions each
dose_and_schedule: Not applicable (descriptive)
mechanism: EGFRvIII is expressed in a subset of cells within EGFR-amplified GBM, often in non-overlapping spatial clones with other EGFR variants (vIII, A289V, etc). The intratumoral heterogeneity means that any single-antigen-directed therapy leaves antigen-negative subclones to repopulate the tumor.
key_finding: EGFRvIII positivity is heterogeneous within tumors and between regions in the same tumor — almost always co-existing with EGFRvIII-negative subclones in the same lesion. This is the underlying biology that explains the rindopepimut ACT IV failure and the antigen-loss escape seen in the O'Rourke 2017 CAR-T trial. Single-antigen targeting cannot work without addressing the negative subpopulation.
caveats: Descriptive heterogeneity study — no therapeutic intervention. The clinical implication is structural: any monovalent EGFRvIII therapy (vaccine, ADC, CAR-T) carries built-in resistance. Justifies the move toward dual-target (EGFR + IL13Ra2) and synNotch (E-SYNC) designs.

intervention_label: EGFRvIII on extrachromosomal DNA — dynamic and reversible expression
model_system: Patient-derived GBM cell lines, EGFRvIII+ at baseline; in-vitro EGFR TKI selection; FISH for chromosomal vs extrachromosomal EGFRvIII; xenograft validation
n_units: Multiple patient-derived lines; xenograft n=6-10/arm
dose_and_schedule: Erlotinib and other EGFR TKIs at clinically relevant concentrations
mechanism: EGFRvIII is frequently encoded on extrachromosomal circular DNA (ecDNA), not on the chromosome. Under EGFR TKI pressure, EGFRvIII ecDNA is rapidly lost from the population; on TKI withdrawal, ecDNA EGFRvIII re-amplifies. Resistance is genetic (ecDNA loss) but reversible — the antigen comes back when the selective pressure ends.
key_finding: EGFRvIII ecDNA expression is highly dynamic. TKI exposure suppresses EGFRvIII; drug holiday re-amplifies it. Erlotinib resistance reverses within 72 h of drug withdrawal. The implication for CAR-T and vaccine therapy: antigen loss observed on therapy may be transient rather than durable, opening the door to sequential or pulsed antigen-directed strategies.
caveats: Mostly in-vitro work; the in-vivo dynamics on a clinical timescale are less well-characterized. The paper changed how the field thinks about EGFRvIII heterogeneity — not a stable lineage trait but a population-level fluctuation.

intervention_label: CAN-3110 (rQNestin34.5v.2) — clinical immunoactivation paper
exclusion_reason: Already on the clinical-evidence ledger (gbm-mtap-c4bq-can3110-ling-2023-nature). It is the phase 1 readout with immune-correlative tissue work, not a preclinical paper. The dedicated CAN-3110 preclinical toxicology paper (Chouljenko 2020 Mol Ther Methods Clin Dev) is the right preclinical row.

intervention_label: CAN-3110 (rQNestin34.5v.2) preclinical toxicology and design rationale
model_system: Murine intracranial glioma model; non-human primate biodistribution; nestin-promoter glioma vs normal-brain cell selectivity assays
n_units: Mouse cohorts n=8-10/arm; NHP biodistribution n=3
dose_and_schedule: Intratumoral rQNestin34.5v.2 at escalating PFU doses
mechanism: rQNestin34.5v.2 places the neurovirulence gene ICP34.5 under control of the nestin promoter, which is selectively active in high-grade glioma and glioma stem cells. The virus replicates and lyses tumor in nestin-expressing cells, while normal CNS cells (which don't drive the nestin promoter) restrict ICP34.5 expression and avoid neurovirulence.
key_finding: rQNestin34.5v.2 was cytotoxic for all tested glioma cell lines (cell survival <20% of control) while sparing nestin-low normal CNS cells. Mouse and non-human primate biodistribution showed restricted replication in nestin-active tissue. The toxicology package supported the IND for the NCT03152318 phase 1.
caveats: Nestin expression is not glioma-specific (also expressed in neural stem cells and some adult progenitors) — the safety margin comes from differential promoter activity, not absolute selectivity. The preclinical toxicology package is the most thorough in the modern oncolytic-HSV space and is the backstop for the clinical Nature 2023 readout.

intervention_label: PVSRIPO mechanism — CD155-targeted oncolysis and myeloid immunoactivation
model_system: Human dendritic cell and macrophage cultures; CD155-expressing tumor lines (glioma, melanoma); ex-vivo tumor explants
n_units: Multiple human DC and macrophage donors; cell lines in replicate
control_arm: Wild-type poliovirus; CD155-negative cells; non-replicating virus
dose_and_schedule: PVSRIPO at varying MOI; sublethal infection of antigen-presenting cells
mechanism: PVSRIPO is a recombinant poliovirus chimera with the internal ribosomal entry site swapped from rhinovirus type 2, ablating neuropathogenicity. CD155 (the poliovirus receptor) is ectopically expressed on glioma cells and constitutively expressed on glioma-associated macrophages and microglia. Sublethal infection of CD155+ antigen-presenting cells produces sustained type-I-interferon-dominant activation.
key_finding: Sublethal PVSRIPO infection of CD155+ dendritic cells and macrophages produced sustained type-I-IFN-dominant activation and primed antigen-specific CTL responses against tumor neoantigens. The dual mechanism (direct lysis of tumor cells + immune-priming of antigen-presenting cells) is the proposed reason for the long-tail responder pattern seen clinically in the Desjardins 2018 NEJM phase 1.
caveats: Mechanism paper, mostly in-vitro. The in-vivo confirmation of myeloid activation came later (Mosaheb 2020 Neuro-Oncology). The CD155 expression data is the part to read carefully — broad CD155 expression on tumor and myeloid cells is exactly what you want, but it is not glioma-specific.

intervention_label: M032 — oncolytic HSV-1 expressing IL-12 (preclinical)
model_system: Aotus non-human primate intracerebral inoculation; mouse intracranial tumor models; biodistribution + neurovirulence safety
n_units: NHP n=3-6 per dose; mouse efficacy n=8-10/arm
control_arm: Parental HSV-1; vehicle; G207 head-to-head in some experiments
dose_and_schedule: Intracerebral M032 dose escalation from 1e6 to 1e8 PFU
mechanism: M032 is a γ134.5-deleted HSV-1 carrying a transgene encoding murine or human IL-12. Tumor-restricted replication kills tumor cells directly; IL-12 secreted locally activates NK and T cells and shifts the tumor microenvironment toward a Th1 program.
key_finding: M032 was non-pathogenic in Aotus NHPs across the full dose range and produced durable tumor regression in mouse intracranial models. IL-12 expression was confirmed in tumor tissue but not in normal brain — the local IL-12 payload is what differentiates M032 from G207 (its non-armed predecessor). The toxicology package supported the human phase 1 (NCT02062827).
caveats: Aotus is the standard primate model for HSV neurovirulence but is not a perfect human predictor. Mouse efficacy used implanted tumor lines, not GEMMs. M032 is conceptually attractive (IL-12 locally) but has not yet shown the clinical signal that CAN-3110 has — phase 1 readout pending.

intervention_label: DNX-2401 / Delta-24-RGD oncolytic adenovirus — clinical with mechanism context
exclusion_reason: Clinical phase 1 paper with mechanism backdrop, not a preclinical paper. DNX-2401 is not on the patient's intervention list (not in trials.jsonl or clinical_evidence.jsonl) — including a preclinical row for it would be off-scope. Logged as audit trail; the broader oncolytic-virus class is covered by CAN-3110 and PVSRIPO preclinical rows.

intervention_label: Depatux-m (ABT-414, EGFR-directed ADC) preclinical
model_system: EGFR-amplified and EGFRvIII+ GBM PDX panel; non-EGFR-amplified controls; xenograft and orthotopic
n_units: Multiple PDX lines; n=8-10 mice/arm
control_arm: Isotype-control ADC; vehicle; head-to-head with temozolomide
dose_and_schedule: Depatux-m IV 3-10 mg/kg, dose-dependent regression studies
mechanism: Depatux-m is an antibody-drug conjugate: the antibody portion (ABT-806) is selective for activated or amplified EGFR including EGFRvIII; the payload is monomethyl auristatin F (MMAF), a microtubule disruptor. EGFR-amplified tumors internalize the ADC, MMAF kills the cell, and bystander effects extend to nearby cells with lower EGFR.
key_finding: Depatux-m produced regressions in EGFR-amplified GBM PDX models including EGFRvIII-positive lines. Activity was strictly EGFR-amplification-dependent — non-amplified controls did not respond. Synergy with temozolomide was observed in head-to-head xenograft studies, motivating the INTELLANCE-1 design.
caveats: Strong preclinical signal, negative phase 3 (INTELLANCE-1, Lassman 2023). Classic example of preclinical-to-clinical mismatch — the ocular toxicity from MMAF and the heterogeneous EGFR expression in real human GBM both limited clinical effect. Logged here as the canonical preclinical-to-clinical caution for the EGFR-ADC class.

intervention_label: CSF-1R inhibition reshapes glioma myeloid microenvironment (TME context)
model_system: PDGFB-driven RCAS GEMM glioma; CSF-1R inhibitor PLX3397; orthotopic transplant models
n_units: n=8-12 mice/arm; multiple GEMM cohorts
dose_and_schedule: PLX3397 oral, continuous dosing
mechanism: Tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) in glioma express CSF-1R and are educated by glioma-derived CSF1 toward an M2-like, immunosuppressive phenotype. CSF-1R blockade does not deplete macrophages but reprograms them toward an antitumor program — reducing IL-10, TGF-β, and Arg1, increasing MHC-II and IFN-γ-responsive genes.
key_finding: PLX3397 produced durable regressions in PDGFB-driven glioma GEMM by reprogramming TAMs rather than depleting them. Survival was extended substantially. The paper is the canonical demonstration that the myeloid compartment is the dominant immunosuppressive node in glioma — more so than T-cell-intrinsic checkpoints.
caveats: PDGFB-driven GEMM is a proneural-subtype model; the same logic may not hold for mesenchymal GBM. Clinical translation has been disappointing — the Butowski / Quail follow-up work showed adaptive PI3K reactivation in TAMs after long-term PLX3397, blunting durable benefit. The mechanism evidence is the part to carry forward: it is the strongest published reason why generic checkpoint inhibition fails in GBM, and why myeloid-targeted combinations are the next move.

intervention_label: Dynamic macrophage repopulation after RT — CSF-1R as a resistance node
model_system: PDGFB-driven glioma GEMM with fractionated cranial RT; CSF-1R blockade combined with RT
n_units: n=8-12 mice/arm across multiple GEMM cohorts
dose_and_schedule: Cranial RT 10 Gy in 2 Gy fractions ± PLX3397 oral
mechanism: After RT, monocyte-derived macrophages repopulate the tumor and adopt a wound-healing / pro-tumorigenic program that drives recurrence. CSF-1R blockade during the post-RT window blocks this repopulation and prevents the resistance trajectory.
key_finding: Adding CSF-1R blockade to RT in PDGFB GEMM glioma extended survival far beyond either modality alone. The post-RT macrophage influx was identified as a tractable resistance node — same biology as the immune-suppressive TME in untreated tumors but kinetically amplified after radiation injury.
caveats: GEMM models — clinical translation of the CSF-1R + RT concept has not yet shown a definitive phase 2/3 signal. Mechanism is the part to carry forward: it explains why standard RT in GBM almost always leads to recurrence with an adaptive immune escape that the patient's IDH-WT GBM will face on its Stupp track.

intervention_label: PRMT5 + CDK4/6 combination — preclinical synergy (cross-tumor with GBM implications)
model_system: Melanoma cell lines and PDX (MTAP status mixed); CDK4/6 inhibitor (palbociclib) + PRMT5 inhibitor (GSK3326595) in vitro and in vivo; MDM4 splicing as molecular endpoint
n_units: Multiple lines and PDX; n=8-10 mice/arm in vivo
dose_and_schedule: Palbociclib + GSK3326595 oral, combination at clinically relevant doses
mechanism: CDK4/6 inhibition indirectly suppresses PRMT5 activity through cell-cycle-dependent regulation of PRMT5 cofactors; PRMT5 in turn regulates MDM4 pre-mRNA splicing, which controls p53 activity. The MDM4 axis links the two enzymes — dual inhibition converges on p53 reactivation and synthetic lethality.
key_finding: Combined palbociclib + GSK3326595 produced deeper and more durable regressions than either agent alone in melanoma models, and delayed emergence of CDK4/6i resistance. The MDM4-p53 axis was the proposed convergent node. Subsequent work in breast cancer (Wang 2024 Nat Commun PMID 38493145) extended the same logic to ER+/Rb-deficient tumors.
caveats: Melanoma, not GBM. The biology — MDM4 splicing and p53 reactivation — is general but the GBM-specific test has not been done in published preclinical work. Relevant to the case because TNG462 has reported preclinical combination signals with CDK4/6 inhibitors in MTAP-null preclinical models (AACR 2025 abstract 2996), and a PRMT5i + CDK4/6i combination in CDKN2A/MTAP co-deleted GBM is the most mechanistically attractive doublet on this patient's chart.

intervention_label: PRMT5 inhibition + temozolomide — preclinical synergy in glioma
journal: Research Square (preprint; Cell Death & Disease in press)
model_system: Patient-derived GBM neurospheres; orthotopic mouse xenograft
n_units: Multiple neurosphere lines; n=8-10 mice/arm in vivo
dose_and_schedule: LLY-283 (PRMT5i, brain-penetrant) + TMZ at clinically relevant doses; sequential and concurrent schedules tested
mechanism: PRMT5 methylates components of the Fanconi anemia / homologous recombination DNA-repair machinery. PRMT5 inhibition impairs HR-mediated repair of TMZ-induced O6-methylguanine and double-strand-break intermediates, increasing TMZ cytotoxicity in MGMT-low or MGMT-methylated tumors and partially rescuing benefit even in MGMT-unmethylated lines.
key_finding: LLY-283 + TMZ in GBM neurospheres produced increased apoptosis (caspase 3/7), more γH2AX foci, and more comet-tail DNA damage than TMZ alone. In orthotopic xenografts, the combination significantly prolonged survival over either single agent. The mechanism is HR repair failure rather than MGMT-pathway interaction.
caveats: Research Square preprint as of data cut; peer-reviewed version pending in Cell Death & Disease. The HR-repair mechanism is the part most likely to generalize across MGMT subgroups; the survival signal will need replication beyond the originating lab. Directly relevant to the patient's pending MGMT result — if unmethylated, PRMT5i + TMZ becomes a mechanism-supported combination even when MGMT methylation is not driving TMZ benefit on its own.

intervention_label: CDK4/6 + temozolomide in glioma — retracted paper
journal: Journal of Cellular and Molecular Medicine
exclusion_reason: Paper was retracted post-publication for image-integrity concerns. The published mechanistic claim (TMZ-induced p-Rb reversed by abemaciclib) is plausible but the data backing the survival numbers is not reliable. Excluded from synthesis. The same combination logic is supported by Raub 2015 (orthotopic abemaciclib activity) and is being tested empirically in INSIGhT.

intervention_label: Bevacizumab vascular and tumor-cell effects in GBM (dose-dependent)
model_system: U87 and U251 GBM xenografts and orthotopic intracranial models; dose-ranging anti-VEGF (bevacizumab)
n_units: n=8-10 mice/arm across dose levels
dose_and_schedule: Bevacizumab IV at 1, 5, and 10 mg/kg twice weekly
mechanism: Bevacizumab binds and neutralizes VEGF-A, blocking VEGF-receptor signaling on tumor endothelium. The effects are dose-dependent: low doses normalize vasculature (improving perfusion and possibly oxygenation); higher doses regress vessels and produce tumor cell apoptosis but compromise downstream drug delivery and increase hypoxia-driven invasive escape.
key_finding: Medium-dose bevacizumab regressed glioma vasculature and tumor growth in orthotopic models, while higher doses produced more vascular destruction but did not further extend survival — the therapeutic window has an upper edge. Tumor-cell-intrinsic effects (VEGFR signaling on tumor cells) accounted for part of the activity, not only vascular normalization.
caveats: Xenograft, not GEMM. The clinical bevacizumab story (no OS benefit in newly diagnosed GBM, modest PFS gain in recurrent) is consistent with the preclinical hint that vascular regression alone is insufficient. The intracranial hemorrhage caveat in this case (patient presented with intratumoral hemorrhage) is not directly tested here but is implicit in the vascular-disruption mechanism.

intervention_label: Microenvironmental atlas of brain tumor myeloid compartment (IDH-WT bias)
model_system: Human brain tumor resections (gliomas IDH-WT and IDH-mutant, brain metastases); flow cytometry, RNA-seq, mass cytometry across 119 patients
n_units: 119 patients across glioma subtypes and brain metastasis
control_arm: Brain metastases and IDH-mutant glioma as biology comparators
dose_and_schedule: Not applicable (descriptive)
mechanism: IDH-WT GBM is dominated by tissue-resident microglia and monocyte-derived macrophages that express immunosuppressive markers (TGFBI, CD163, MARCO) and lack the activation signatures seen in IDH-mutant tumors or brain metastases. T cells are sparse and exhausted; the dominant immune-cell pool is myeloid.
key_finding: IDH-WT GBM has a uniquely myeloid-dominated immune microenvironment with minimal T-cell infiltration — substantially more immunosuppressive than IDH-mutant glioma or brain metastases. The signature predicts why generic PD-1 blockade fails (no T cells to unleash) and why myeloid-targeted strategies (CSF-1R, TGF-β, CD47) and locoregional T-cell delivery (intraventricular CAR-T) are the mechanistically supported alternatives.
caveats: Descriptive immunology — no therapeutic intervention. The IDH-WT vs IDH-mutant contrast is the part most directly relevant to the patient (who is IDH-WT). Justifies the case-level skepticism about generic ICI and the case-level interest in neoadjuvant pembrolizumab (Cloughesy 2019) and oncolytic-virus immune priming (CAN-3110).

intervention_label: PVSRIPO drives diffuse microglia activation across the CNS (immune-priming mechanism)
model_system: Mouse intracerebral injection of PVSRIPO; immunohistochemistry and scRNA-seq of microglia and infiltrating myeloid cells
n_units: Mouse cohorts n=6-10/group; multiple time points post-injection
dose_and_schedule: Single intracerebral PVSRIPO injection
mechanism: PVSRIPO triggers diffuse, sustained microglial activation extending well beyond the injection site through the CNS. The activation is type-I-interferon-dominant and persists for weeks, providing a prolonged immunostimulatory window in which adaptive antitumor responses can develop.
key_finding: A single intratumoral PVSRIPO injection drove diffuse microglia activation through the CNS for weeks, with type-I-IFN gene signatures persisting beyond the local injection site. The finding explains the long-tail clinical responder pattern (Desjardins 2018 21% 24-month OS plateau) — the response is not from acute lysis alone but from delayed myeloid-driven adaptive immunity.
caveats: Mouse work — the human translation rests on CSF and tumor analysis from clinical samples, which the Brown/Gromeier group has begun publishing separately. The mechanism is the most coherent published explanation for why PVSRIPO has long-tail benefit despite a modest median-OS signal.

intervention_label: TNG462 + CDK4/6 inhibitor in MTAP-null preclinical models (AACR 2025)
model_system: MTAP-null CDX and PDX panel (NSCLC, pancreatic, bladder); TNG462 ± palbociclib or abemaciclib combination dosing
n_units: Multiple PDX lines; n=8-10 mice/arm
dose_and_schedule: Oral TNG462 + oral palbociclib or abemaciclib at clinically achievable doses
mechanism: TNG462 inhibits PRMT5 selectively in MTAP-null cells; CDK4/6 inhibitors block Rb phosphorylation. The combination converges on G1/S blockade through two distinct nodes — PRMT5-dependent splicing of cell-cycle genes plus direct cyclin-D/CDK4/6 inhibition. Particularly attractive in MTAP+CDKN2A co-deleted tumors (the 9p21 co-deletion phenotype the patient carries).
key_finding: TNG462 + CDK4/6 inhibitor produced deeper and more durable regressions than either agent alone across MTAP-null PDX models. The combination was tolerated and showed clear additivity in MTAP+CDKN2A co-deleted lines — the sponsor explicitly nominated this as a development path for GBM (using a CNS-penetrant PRMT5i in place of TNG462, since TNG462 itself does not cross the BBB).
caveats: Conference abstract — full peer-reviewed manuscript pending. No GBM cohort in the actual preclinical models tested; the GBM development path is the sponsor's stated intent, not yet executed. Still the most directly relevant preclinical combination data for this patient's MTAP+CDKN2A co-deletion phenotype.

intervention_label: Rindopepimut — phase 2 with immune-escape mechanism (ACTIVATE / ACT II)
model_system: EGFRvIII+ newly diagnosed GBM patients (n=18 ACTIVATE) with paired pre/post-vaccine tumor sampling; mouse intracerebral SMA-560 efficacy backdrop
n_units: n=18 vaccinated patients with paired tumor sampling at recurrence
dose_and_schedule: PEPvIII (KLH-conjugated EGFRvIII peptide) intradermal + GM-CSF; q2w priming then monthly maintenance
mechanism: Synthetic 14-mer peptide spanning the EGFRvIII fusion junction conjugated to KLH, given with GM-CSF adjuvant. Generates EGFRvIII-specific antibodies and T cells. Mechanism of failure: vaccinated patients lost EGFRvIII expression at recurrence, demonstrating immune-driven antigen escape in human tumors.
key_finding: EGFRvIII expression was lost in 82% of recurrent tumors from vaccinated patients vs persistent expression in untreated controls. The paper coined the 'immunologic escape' framing for EGFRvIII vaccines. mPFS ~14.2 mo and mOS ~26 mo were encouraging in single-arm context; phase 3 ACT IV later showed the OS benefit did not survive blinded comparison — heterogeneous EGFRvIII allows antigen-negative subclones to escape.
caveats: Logged primarily as a board-relevant caution: strong preclinical signal + positive phase 2 + negative phase 3. The antigen-loss biology (Snuderl 2011, Nathanson 2014) was the proximate failure mechanism. The same lesson informs the patient's EGFRvIII CAR-T trial selection — dual-target and synNotch designs are the post-rindopepimut response.

intervention_label: Toca 511 retroviral cytosine deaminase + 5-FC preclinical
exclusion_reason: Toca 511 program is discontinued (TOCA 5 phase 3 was negative; sponsor Tocagen wound down). The preclinical signal was strong (durable CR in orthotopic models) but the clinical translation failed and the drug is not enrollable. Logged as audit trail for the oncolytic / gene-therapy axis; relevant context for why CAN-3110 and PVSRIPO are the current active assets, not Toca 511.

intervention_label: PRMT5 synthetic lethality in MTAP-deficient GBM — review
exclusion_reason: Review article, not primary preclinical data. The primary papers it synthesizes are already captured in the included rows (Kryukov 2016, Mavrakis 2016, Marjon 2016, Sachamitr 2021, Engstrom 2024, Smith 2023, Kalev 2021).

intervention_label: IDE397 — second-generation MAT2A inhibitor (preclinical and early clinical)
model_system: MTAP-null CDX and PDX panel (NSCLC, urothelial, esophageal, mesothelioma); biochemical and cellular MAT2A inhibition; SAM depletion as PD readout
n_units: Multiple PDX lines, n=8-10 mice/arm
dose_and_schedule: Oral IDE397, daily, dose titrated to plasma SAM suppression
mechanism: IDE397 is an allosteric MAT2A inhibitor that blocks SAM synthesis in MTAP-null cells. Lower SAM (combined with elevated MTA from MTAP loss) collapses residual PRMT5 activity past the lethal threshold. Designed for better DMPK properties than first-generation AG-270.
key_finding: IDE397 produced regressions across MTAP-null PDX lineages (urothelial, NSCLC dominant) and reduced plasma SAM in a dose-dependent manner that tracks tumor response. Clinical phase 1 expansion at 30 mg QD reported 33% ORR in evaluable MTAP-null urothelial / NSCLC patients (8 PR + 1 CR in n=27).
caveats: No CNS-specific exposure data published. IDEAYA's GBM strategy depends on the IDE892 successor (still phase 1, no GBM cohort yet) or the IDE397 + anvumetostat combination (NCT05975073, completed) — the GBM relevance of IDE397 is the mechanism class, not the molecule. Logged because the broader MAT2A axis is part of the case's targetable feature mapping.
